scope: Recoverable explicit folder-source purge through REST, CLI and browser; not full M4 acceptance
verifiedBehavior: Persisted intent stops source admissions, clears pending scans and cancels processing before file removal.
Source admission and purge share a per-source gate; an in-flight import completes before its retained bytes are purged.
Late processing publication and document mutation are fenced while a source purge is pending.
Owned originals, historical copies and trash are removed in bounded journal batches while external originals remain.
An older interrupted document mutation is settled before sweeping its files.
Injected file-removal and index-publication interruptions recover after the initiating credential is revoked, without duplicate purge revisions.
Purge supports sources already removed and sources with no documents. The built-in inbox remains protected.
A fixture with 1100 historical files plus a current original is purged while an unrelated file remains.
Unsafe owned links leave a sanitized pending failure; other roots are purged and repair permits recovery.
Calendar roots, members, occurrence coverage and payload lineage are purged with their folder source.
Both API route prefixes require an admin session and recent password confirmation; API-key requests are rejected.
Desktop and phone workflows cover cancellation, explicit confirmation, retained tombstone counts and unavailable content. Fixture shutdown verifies external originals still exist.
notes: Initial builds caught local-variable and test-property naming errors before functional tests ran.

The first API fixture stopped the folder worker during startup and exposed unhandled cancellation that shut down the host. Cancellation across startup and the loop is now handled; both API tests and the full server regression passed afterward.

The initial browser fixture required embedding completion even though extraction was already complete and searchable. Its readiness check now verifies extracted text and accepts the documented indexed_partial state. Only the qualification fixture changed after the full regression; its final run passed.
All four final screenshots were visually reviewed. Browser errors and warnings were zero, and the fixture stopped successfully.
No golden snapshots or model evaluation recordings needed updates for this checkpoint.
limitations: Large-corpus end-to-end latency has not been qualified. Work uses bounded document pages and file batches; that alone is not a performance guarantee.
Unreadable, linked or conflicting owned files leave a durable pending purge until repaired.
Direct standalone container-document purge retains the earlier 1000-removal/64-KiB journal bounds; source-wide purges use bounded file batches.
Debug-log cleanup, backup rotation, encrypted backup/restore/export, enrichment/provider/budget, release and real-export acceptance remain open.
Versioned M4 migrations and hardened production deployment remain open. No production service, data or configuration changed.
